product.title: The problem and the product
product.takeaway: Teams shipping AI in Europe need answers they can check, in their own language.

problem.head: Two long regulations
problem.text: AI Act: 113 articles, 13 annexes, 180 recitals. GDPR: 99 articles, 173 recitals.

problem.head: Unverifiable chatbots
problem.text: Generic chat-with-PDF answers cannot be checked, and they rarely refuse.

problem.head: Bilingual teams
problem.text: French and English readers need the same answer, citing the same article.

solution.head: Cited Q&A
solution.text: Every rule ends with an article ID that was actually retrieved, shown as "AI Act, Art. 6(2)".

solution.head: Risk-tier classifier
solution.text: Describe a system, get prohibited, high risk, transparency, minimal or needs more info.

solution.head: Where teams work
solution.text: REST API, Slack, MCP clients and a Google Sheets register.

product.users: Users: compliance officers and DPOs, product managers, ML engineers. Information only, never legal advice.
product.notes: For a non-technical audience: the product promise is checkable answers. Every rule cites an article that was actually retrieved, and the system refuses rather than guesses. It is information, never legal advice.

architecture.title: Architecture: built vs planned
architecture.takeaway: One API serves every client. Today the offline ingestion path exists; everything downstream is planned.
architecture.notes: Three layers. The offline pipeline is built: EUR-Lex pages, the parser and chunker, and chunks.jsonl. Serving and clients are planned. Every client is a thin HTTP client of one FastAPI service, which keeps integrations testable.

metric_tree.title: What success means
metric_tree.takeaway: One proposed north star, four drivers we can move, four guardrails we must not break.

north_star.name: Trusted answer rate
north_star.definition: Share of questions where ActWise either answers with only verified, faithful citations, or correctly refuses.
north_star.note: Proposed. Definition to confirm once the judge is calibrated (Step 6).

metric_tree.companion: Companion metric for the classifier: tier accuracy ≥ 85%, and 0 prohibited systems labelled minimal risk.
metric_tree.notes: As product data scientist I propose one north star: the trusted answer rate. It rewards answering with verified, faithful citations and rewards correct refusals. Drivers are what we tune; guardrails are hard limits.

eval_design.title: How we will measure
eval_design.takeaway: Split first, then build data, then score at article level. The order is what prevents leakage.

steps.head: Split by article
steps.text: 70 / 15 / 15 with seed 42. Train articles feed fine-tuning only; test numbers are the ones reported.

steps.head: Golden set
steps.text: 50 hand-written questions (15+ in French, 5 types), then 100 synthetic ones reviewed by hand.

steps.head: Retrieval metrics
steps.text: Recall@5, MRR@10, nDCG@10 at article level, so windows of one article count once.

steps.head: Generation metrics
steps.text: Faithfulness judge checked against 60 human labels (kappa ≥ 0.6), citation precision, refusals.

steps.head: Gates
steps.text: Retrieval eval on every PR, fail on a 2-point drop. LLM eval weekly, in slices, from a disk cache.

eval_design.footnote: Leakage guard: test_no_split_leakage fails if any dev or test article appears in the fine-tuning pairs.
eval_design.notes: The order matters: split by article first, so no text from a test article leaks into training pairs or prompt tuning. Metrics are at article level so overlapping windows of one article count once.

corpus.title: Corpus: complete in both languages
corpus.takeaway: Every official recital, article and annex was found in English and French, with identical ID sets.
corpus.note: Source: EUR-Lex, saved 2026-10-04. The AI Act text is the 2024 original, without the AI Omnibus (Reg. 2026/1744).
corpus.notes: Every official recital, article and annex was found in both languages. The French corpus has more chunks because French text is longer, but the paragraph-level ID sets are identical.

chunk_finding.title: Finding: long paragraphs dominate
chunk_finding.takeaway: Over a third of all chunks are overlapping windows. Retrieval must not let one paragraph fill the top 5.
implications: Deduplicate windows of the same paragraph before cutting to top-k (tests H4).
Metrics already count an article once, so the effect hides in recall but shows in context quality.
French text runs longer, so French questions see more fragments (part of H3).
chunk_finding.notes: Over a third of chunks are windows of long paragraphs. Article-level metrics hide duplicates, but the model would see five fragments of one paragraph instead of five different sources. That is hypothesis H4.

edge_cases.title: Finding: real text broke the reference parser
edge_cases.takeaway: Six edge cases the guide's parser missed. Each one is now pinned by a test on the real pages.

items.case: FR preamble ends with "ONT ADOPTÉ", not "ONT ARRÊTÉ"
Footnote marks broken across several lines inside the text
Signatures, footnotes and footer after the body
Annexes VIII and XI restart their numbering
items.fix: Points become b.1, 2.1 with clear labels

edge_cases.lesson: Lesson: test on the real documents from day one. The sample text passed; the real pages did not.
edge_cases.notes: The reference parser passed the sample text but missed six patterns on the real pages. Each fix is pinned by a test, and tests/test_corpus.py checks the official counts on every run.

decisions.title: Decisions and code review
decisions.takeaway: One decision recorded. Ten defects found in the reference code: two fixed, one partly fixed.

adr_notes.001-chunking.md: Why: paragraph-level citations are what a lawyer checks, and shared IDs let French questions be scored against the same gold labels. Revisit if fixed windows retrieve as well in Step 4.

review.text: Shared EN/FR IDs overwrite chunks in stores
Stripping an invented ID damages valid ones
LLM cache key ignores model names
Retries delay failover past Cloud Run limits
Daily cap counts per instance (2x real cap)
80% coverage gate vs untested glue code
master vs main breaks the deploy trigger
Retry test expects the wrong delays

decisions.notes: One decision record so far: structure-aware chunking with language-free IDs. The review of the reference code found ten defects; R8 and R9 are fixed, R1 is half fixed and finishes when indexing lands in Step 4.

risks.title: Risks and mitigations
risks.takeaway: The biggest near-term risk is statistical: too few dev questions to see real differences.

items.head: Too few eval questions
items.text: 50 questions spread 70/15/15 leave about 8 on dev: one question moves Recall@5 by 12 points.
items.mitigation: Write 20+ questions each on dev and test articles; report n and bootstrap intervals.

items.head: Free tiers change
items.text: Gemini and Groq quotas can shrink without notice and stall evals or the demo.
items.mitigation: Disk cache, provider fallback, daily cap, eval in slices.

items.head: Synthetic questions flatter
items.text: A model tuned on LLM-written questions may look better on LLM-written questions.
items.mitigation: Report hand-written and synthetic results separately.

items.head: Law moved on
items.text: The AI Omnibus (Reg. 2026/1744) shifts Annex III dates; the corpus is the 2024 text.
items.mitigation: State it in the model card; corpus versioning as a stretch goal.

items.head: Users over-trust answers
items.text: A cited answer can still be read as legal advice.
items.mitigation: Refuse when unsure, no compliance verdicts, disclaimer on every result.

items.head: Silent data loss
items.text: Shared EN/FR IDs would let French chunks overwrite English ones in stores (R1).
items.mitigation: Storage key id@lang added in Step 2; enforce it when indexing.

risks.notes: The highest risk is measurement, not engineering: too few questions per split to see real differences. The mitigation is cheap: write questions on purpose for dev and test articles and report intervals.
